mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (at or below 0.25%) indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
evidence_refs: doc:Federal Reserve Policy Response to Great Recession
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS <= 0.25% (p-value < 0.05 for negative returns), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 9.5% signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce household income and consumer spending, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE > 9.5% (p-value < 0.05 for positive returns), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 1% each month indicates a severe contraction in consumer demand, which triggers a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:Both HOUST and RSAFS declined in July 2009
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered instances (HOUST and RSAFS both down >1%), or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p-value > 0.05) in a regression of returns on the interaction term.

mechanism_narrative: During the post-recession recovery phase, a sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 6-month moving average indicates strengthening manufacturing activity, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods classified as 'post-recession recovery' when INDPRO is rising, or the regime-specific Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in retail sales (RSAFS) above its 3-month moving average indicates strong consumer spending, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when RSAFS is rising (above 3-month MA), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) annual change above 2.5% signals rising inflation expectations that prompt the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL annual change > 2.5%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in housing starts (HOUST) and non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 0.5% each month indicates a broad-based economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:Both HOUST and PAYEMS declined in July 2009
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered instances (HOUST and PAYEMS both down >0.5%), or the interaction effect is not significant (p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 6-month moving average signals weakening manufacturing output, which causes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when INDPRO < 6-month MA, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
